speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development what is the progress of the three-year pilot to provide infant childminding services that was announced earlier this year.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that childminding services can be a popular work choice with return-to-work women due to the flexibility of the work, what plans does the Ministry have to reach out to more women groups and the Labour Movement on promoting this as a viable work option?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And what would be some of the successful endpoints for this pilot?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Is there a golden ratio of childminders to population size, for instance?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To answer her last question first, like I mentioned, the intent we are looking at through this pilot is we are looking to provide an affordable, safe service for infants, a service that is trusted by families with infants.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, the pilot is to test whether there is a market for this service.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I shared, we are in the midst of discussing with the operators to appoint the appropriate operator.
